description: Our product is a 25 mm foil-faced polyiso board meant to go on the outside of 2x6 walls with R-20 batts, as continuous insulation under the siding. The foil makes it essentially vapour-impermeable. A builder in Edmonton was told the outboard insulation is too thin for that wall. We think the foil is fine because the joints are taped. How do we make the case?

missing_info.field: complete layer order, measured material thermal resistances and innermost impermeable surface
missing_info.why: Thickness and batt label alone do not establish the outboard-to-inboard ratio.

missing_info.field: air leakage, dry-cup vapour permeance and design heating degree-days
missing_info.why: Establish applicability, exceptions and the tabulated ratio without assuming product properties.

missing_info.field: whether a vented air space is inboard of the low-permeance board
missing_info.why: The material must be outboard of that air space for the vented-space option.
